short_bio: Associate Justice of the Supreme Court since 1991.
biography:
Clarence Thomas was born in Pin Point, Georgia, studied at Holy Cross and took his law degree at Yale in 1974. He worked for Missouri’s attorney general and later at Monsanto, then in the Reagan administration, where he chaired the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission from 1982.

George H. W. Bush appointed him to the DC Circuit in 1990 and nominated him to the Supreme Court in 1991. After hearings that included testimony from Anita Hill, the Senate confirmed him 52–48.

He is known for an originalist reading of the Constitution and wrote the memoir My Grandfather’s Son (2007).
